Assistant recommended setting aside one weekend day to prep ingredients for the week ahead
Assistant recommended deciding meals for the week and making a grocery list to avoid last-minute takeout
Assistant recommended preparing lunch the night before or morning of to avoid relying on delivery services
Assistant suggested sliced bananas, berries (strawberries, blueberries, raspberries), diced apples, or dried fruits (cranberries, apricots, raisins) as oat toppings
Assistant suggested chia seeds (omega-3s, protein, fiber, gel-like texture) and flaxseeds (nutty flavor, omega-3s, fiber) as oat toppings
Assistant suggested unsweetened coconut flakes for a creamy, tropical flavor
Assistant suggested cinnamon, cocoa powder, or vanilla extract/bean as oat toppings
Assistant suggested drizzling honey, maple syrup, or fruit preserves (strawberry or blueberry) for sweetness
Assistant suggested mixing in Greek yogurt for extra creaminess and a protein boost
Assistant suggested peanut butter or sunflower seed butter for rich, satisfying flavor
Assistant suggested tahini or hemp seed butter for creaminess, plus shredded coconut or shaved dark chocolate

Assistant gave a recipe: 1/2 cup rolled oats, 1/2 cup unsweetened almond milk or milk of choice, 1 tablespoon chia seeds, 1 tablespoon honey or maple syrup (optional), pinch of salt; refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight (8-10 hours)

Assistant advised stirring well to distribute chia seeds, noting they absorb liquid and thicken overnight; use less chia or more milk for creamier texture; can add vanilla extract, cinnamon, or protein powder
Assistant said to replace the 1 tablespoon of chia seeds with 1 tablespoon of ground flaxseeds; flaxseeds have a slightly nutty flavor and coarser texture
Assistant said a coffee grinder works great for grinding flaxseeds: add seeds and pulse until desired consistency
Assistant said a high-powered blender like a Vitamix or Blendtec can grind flaxseeds with short pulses, avoiding over-blending
Assistant said a food processor can grind flaxseeds in short pulses
Assistant said a mortar and pestle can grind flaxseeds with more effort for a fine grind
Assistant advised grinding flaxseeds just before using (they go rancid if ground too far in advance), grinding in small batches, and sifting to remove large pieces
Assistant noted pre-ground flaxseeds can be purchased at most health food stores or online
Assistant suggested a cilantro lime dressing: freshly chopped cilantro, lime juice, olive oil, garlic, and a pinch of salt
Assistant suggested roasted diced bell peppers, onions, and jalapeños with olive oil, salt, and pepper for a spicy kick
Assistant suggested grilled pineapple pieces for caramelized sweetness complementing the savory quinoa and chicken
Assistant suggested an avocado crema: mashed ripe avocado with lime juice, salt, and a pinch of cumin
Assistant suggested sprinkling crumbled feta cheese on top for a salty, tangy element
Assistant suggested toasting cumin and coriander seeds in a dry pan, grinding, and sprinkling over the salad for depth
Assistant suggested diced chipotle peppers in adobo sauce for smoky heat
Assistant suggested using flavorful grilled chicken breast such as chipotle-lime or fajita-style
Assistant suggested adding chopped fresh herbs (parsley, basil, cilantro), trying tri-color or red quinoa, and adding chopped hard-boiled eggs, diced tomatoes, or sliced black olives
Assistant recommended marinating chicken breast in olive oil, acid (lime juice or vinegar), and spices for at least 30 minutes to an hour
Assistant recommended soaking chicken breast in a saltwater brine (1 tablespoon salt per 1 cup water) for 30 minutes to an hour before grilling to keep it moist
Assistant recommended gently pounding the chicken breast to an even thickness for consistent cooking
Assistant recommended grilling chicken breast at medium-low heat (around 325°F to 350°F) to prevent burning the outside
Assistant advised against pressing down on the chicken breast with a spatula, as it squeezes out juices and dries the meat
Assistant advised ensuring chicken breast reaches an internal temperature of 165°F for food safety
Assistant recommended letting cooked chicken breast rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing to redistribute juices
Assistant suggested pan-searing chicken breast in a hot skillet with oil and spices for a crispy crust and juicy interior
Assistant suggested oven roasting chicken breast with aromatics like onions, carrots, and celery for a moist result
Assistant suggested poaching chicken breast in broth with aromatics for a tender and juicy result
Assistant suggested Chipotle Lime Chicken: marinate in lime juice, olive oil, chipotle peppers, and cumin
Assistant suggested Herby Chicken: olive oil, minced garlic,chopped herbs (thyme, rosemary, or parsley), salt, and pepper as a rub
Assistant suggested Korean-Style Chicken: marinate in soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and gochujang for sweet and spicy flavor
